answer: The protocol refuses to accept new stake beyond 10% of the pool from any one declared operator, so an attacker cannot buy dominance outright. Because the dawn declaration is reconciled against the jetty funding graph, the ripple audit exposes a hidden operator and its excess is returned without reward. Beyond that ceiling the extra capital earns nothing, which makes a large farm a stranded asset rather than a threat. That is 8 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
